pending_articles.title: Multimodal regulation of neurite extension by extracellular matrix composition and electrical stimulation on aligned collagen fiber scaffolds
pending_articles.content: Objective. Peripheral nerve regeneration is regulated by structural, biochemical, and electrical cues, yet their combined effects on neurite outgrowth remain unclear. In this study, an aligned fibrous scaffold was developed to evaluate how extracellular matrix (ECM) composition and electrical stimulation influence neurite extension and growth cone morphology. Approach. Type I collagen fibers incorporating fibronectin, collagen IV, and laminin I were fabricated by contact drawing. The contact drawn fibers were then consolidated into multifilaments, which were mounted on custom frames for cell culture. Primary dorsal root ganglia (DRG) explants were cultured on the multifilaments, and neurite outgrowth and alignment were quantified as a function of ECM composition. Functional activity was confirmed by patch clamp. High-resolution confocal imaging was performed to assess cytoskeletal organization and growth cone morphology. Electrical stimulation was applied to evaluate interactions between biochemical and bioelectrical cues. Main Results. Collagen multifilament scaffolds promoted a high degree of neurite alignment relative to DRGs cultured on isotropic surfaces. Fibronectin and collagen IV increased neurite length in a concentration-dependent manner, with maximal effects observed at intermediate ligand densities, while laminin I had no significant effect. Combinatorial ECM presentation produced non-additive responses. Electrical stimulation increased neurite length on collagen-only scaffolds but had a reduced effect or no effect with incorporation of additional ECM constituents. Growth cone morphology was altered by ECM composition, with fibronectin-, collagen IV-, and combinatorial scaffolds producing less circular growth cones, despite no significant differences in filopodia number or overall morphology-classification proportions. Significance. Neurite extension and growth cone structure are governed by non-linear interactions between multimodal cues. The scaffold system described here facilitates systematic comparison of multiple regenerative cues to inform the design of material for promoting nerve regeneration.

recently_processed.title: A red fluorescent sensor for intensity-and lifetime imaging of cAMP in living cells
recently_processed.content: cAMP (cyclic adenosine monophosphate) is a crucial intracellular messenger involved in neuromodulation and plasticity, but more information on its spatiotemporal regulation is desirable. Here we constructed a red fluorescent indicator based on a truncated cAMP binding site derived from a regulatory PKA subunit of protozoan origin. It contains a single binding site for cAMP highly specific for cAMP over cGMP. chILI (cAMP highly-responsive Intensity and Lifetime Indicator) can be imaged as an intensity-based probe, but alternatively also offers options for fluorescence lifetime imaging. When expressed in the mouse brain using AAV-vector mediated gene transfer, it reports spontaneous and evoked cAMP transients from CA1 neurons in the hippocampus of awake mice. chILI will add valuable options for monitoring cAMP in vitro and in vivo.

recently_processed.title: Digital health meets Parkinson’s disease: a bibliometric exploration of wearable sensors research and emerging frontiers (2005–2026)
recently_processed.content: BackgroundWearable and sensor-based monitoring technologies are increasingly used to support objective, longitudinal assessment in Parkinson’s disease (PD). However, the global development, knowledge structure, and emerging research frontiers of this interdisciplinary field remain incompletely mapped.MethodsBibliographic records on wearable and sensor-based monitoring technologies in PD were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus for the period from 1 January 2005 to 2 February 2026. Searches were conducted in title, abstract, and author keyword fields. Microsoft Excel, VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the bibliometrix R package were used to analyze publication trends, collaboration networks, co-citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, clustering, citation bursts, historiographic patterns, and source impact.ResultsA total of 3,332 publications were included. Publication output increased rapidly over the study period, particularly after 2019, while 2026 represented an incomplete publication year because the search was conducted on 2 February 2026. The United States (U.S.), China, and European countries constituted the main knowledge-production and collaboration structure. Thematic analyses suggested a gradual shift from engineering validation and objective motor-symptom quantification toward AI-enabled digital biomarkers, remote monitoring, multimodal monitoring, and closed-loop neuromodulation. These patterns reflect research activity and citation structures rather than direct evidence of clinical efficacy.ConclusionThis bibliometric analysis provides science-mapping evidence on the evolution of wearable and sensor-based monitoring technologies in PD. Future work should prioritize standardization, multicenter real-world validation, clinical workflow integration, multimodal data fusion, and cautious evaluation of closed-loop applications.

recently_processed.title: Bite-block effects on native s/ʃ and English r/l in child speakers of a language with/without this contrast
recently_processed.content: Learning to produce non-native speech contrasts requires developing new phonological categories as well as new articulatory-perceptual mappings for these new categories. However, within the same speakers, it remains unclear how these new categories compare to contrasts that are already fully established in the native language. To examine potential differences between native and non-native sounds, we recorded Japanese children’s (8–12 years) productions of a non-native contrast (English /ɹ/−/l/, indexed by F3–F2) and a native contrast (/s/−/ʃ/, indexed by Center of Gravity). Recordings were done both under normal speaking conditions and under articulatory perturbation induced by a temporary bite-block while listening to a model. Children acoustically differentiated both contrasts under normal speaking conditions, but the two contrasts showed different developmental profiles: differentiation of the native contrast did not vary with age, whereas differentiation of the non-native contrast was significant only in older children. As expected, the bite-block manipulation reduced acoustic distinctness for both contrasts; however, susceptibility to this disruption was age-invariant for the native contrast but increased with age for the non-native contrast.

recently_processed.title: From biomechanical data to robotic execution: design and control of an intelligent Tuina system
recently_processed.content: IntroductionTraditional Chinese medicine (TCM) Tuina (massage) relies heavily on practitioners' physical stamina and subjective experience, leading to operational variability that hinders therapeutic standardization and scalable rehabilitation service delivery. To address this limitation, this study proposes an intelligent TCM Tuina robotic system integrating biomechanical data-driven design and hybrid control strategies.MethodsA 6-DOF manipulator equipped with a biomimetic end-effector is developed, and a CMPGA-Corr neural network (Convolutional Multi-branch Prototype-Guided Architecture with a Channel-Correlation Branch) is constructed to decouple the spatiotemporal features of nine Tuina manipulations from 25-channel tactile data. Robotic execution is implemented within a Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2)-based control framework. The framework combines RRT-Connect path planning, S-curve speed profiling, and RBF-compensated admittance control. PID, conventional Admittance, and RBF controllers were compared in complete-process simulations using five repetitions per manipulation.ResultsThe RBF controller produced the lowest mean RMSE and MAE for all six evaluated manipulations. Physical experiments on a silicone back phantom further demonstrated bounded and repeatable force-tracking behavior under the tested conditions.DiscussionThe proposed framework bridges TCM practice with modern robotic engineering and provides a scalable and standardized solution for precision rehabilitation robotics.
